headline: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO 11 days after exit
dek: The Guardian, CNBC and Wired report the board reversed course after consulting US officials.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: A fast reversal
body: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, president and board member by unanimous vote, 11 days after he stepped down (The Guardian Technology, CNBC Technology).
Days earlier, the board chair had said it did not intend to bring him back (Wired AI, Engadget).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: What swayed the board
s3.body: The company cites talks with Huang and input from the US government.

points.t: Says it is satisfied with Huang's candor (CNBC Technology).
Nvidia concluded there is no national security risk (Wired AI).
Publicly welcomed the decision (The Guardian Technology).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Markets reacted
body: Shares jumped more than 30% on Monday, per CNBC Technology and Xataka.
Nvidia held roughly 90% of the global GPU market in September (Wired AI).

items.t: The independent investigation stays open (CNBC Technology, Xataka).
Colette Kress returns to her finance role (CNBC Technology).
Outlets don't say if Trump's remarks swayed the board.

caption.hook: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO 11 days after he stepped down.
body: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, president and board member, effective immediately, by unanimous board vote, according to the Guardian, CNBC and Wired. The move came 11 days after his exit and reversed the board chair's remarks that the company did not intend to bring him back (Wired AI, Engadget).

The company says it consulted senior US officials and concluded his return poses no national security risk (Wired AI). The independent investigation stays open, and shares jumped more than 30% on Monday (CNBC Technology, Xataka). The outlets don't say whether Trump swayed the board.
caption.cta: Was the board right to bring Huang back so fast?
